title: How to Store Onions So They Last Longer

content_html:
Whole onions last best in a cool, dry, dark, well-ventilated place. Moisture and sealed bags promote softening and mold, and storing them beside potatoes can speed deterioration; cut onion, however, belongs in the refrigerator.

Give whole onions airflow

Use a basket, mesh bag, or ventilated container rather than a sealed plastic bag. Leave space for air around the bulbs and promptly remove any onion that becomes soft, damp, or moldy.

Choose a dark, relatively cool location

Light and heat encourage sprouting and quality loss. A ventilated pantry works better than a spot beside the oven, dishwasher, or sunny window; avoid damp locations such as under a sink with condensation.

Store onions away from potatoes

Both foods release moisture and compounds that can speed deterioration when stored together in a confined area. Use separate baskets and check weekly so damaged produce is removed before affecting neighboring items.

Refrigerate onion after it is cut

Store halves or pieces in a sealed container or wrap to reduce drying and odor transfer. Keep the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below and discard pieces that become slimy, moldy, or clearly spoiled.

faq.question: Why shouldn't whole onions be kept in a sealed plastic bag?
faq.answer: Use a basket, mesh bag, or ventilated container rather than a sealed plastic bag. Leave space for air around the bulbs and promptly remove any onion that becomes soft, damp, or moldy.

faq.question: Should onions and potatoes be stored together?
faq.answer: Both foods release moisture and compounds that can speed deterioration when stored together in a confined area. Use separate baskets and check weekly so damaged produce is removed before affecting neighboring items.

faq.question: Where should a cut onion be stored?
faq.answer: Store halves or pieces in a sealed container or wrap to reduce drying and odor transfer. Keep the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below and discard pieces that become slimy, moldy, or clearly spoiled.
